newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's QIDC says year profit up 23.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Australia's QIDC says year profit up 23.2 pct.

text.p: State-owned Queensland industry financier QIDC Ltd said on Wednesday it increased net profit by 23.2 percent to A$27.1 million in the year to June 30.

The result was aided by strong lending growth, improving rural conditions and consistent asset quality, QIDC said. Total lending and other receivables grew by A$493.2 million or 23.2 percent to A$2.6 billion from A$2.1 billion while capital and reserves increased by A$14.6 million or seven percent to A$221.9 million, the financier said.
The net profit was equivalent to an after-tax return of 12.6 percent on average capital, it said.
Total income rose by A$60.9 million to A$298.5 million, largely as a result of an increase in receivables.
Chairman Norm Fussell said A$19.5 million had been provided to the Queensland state government, comprising A$10.9 million in dividend payments and A$8.6 million in lieu of income tax.

Fussell said QIDC's 1995/96 profit was an excellent outcome for in view of increased competition in the small to medium business end of the market and fierce competition for the business of large corporates.
"The corporation has experienced aggressive competition from both bank and non-bank providers of business credit over the past 12 months which impacted on gross margins," Fussell said.

"However, improving conditions in some areas of rural Queensland and a sustained business development programme has resulted in a 23.2 percent lift in receivables and a strong profit position," he said in a statement.

Fussell said that despite severe drought conditions still applying in many rural areas, lending to the primary industry sector remained the largest single area of exposure for QIDC at 46 percent of the portfolio or A$1.2 billion.
Lending to secondary industry accounted for A$461.3 or 18 percent of the loan/lease portfolio.
Exposure to Queensland's tertiary industry sector, including construction and developement, tourism and transport, had grown to A$955.4 million or 36 percent of the lending book, he said.
Fussell said QIDC's total assets increased by A$334.3 million or 12 percent to A$3.1 billion over the year.
Total bad and doubtful debt expense for the year was A$2.5 million, comprising a A$2.2 million general provision and A$300,000 in net bad debts written off and specific provisions.
